newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TURKISH BANKS LOSE BID TO REOPEN DUTCH ACCOUNTS.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH BANKS LOSE BID TO REOPEN DUTCH ACCOUNTS.

text.p: A Dutch court has rejected the request of four Turkish banks to force ABN AMRO to reopen their accounts in the Netherlands, which were closed recently, ABN AMRO and the Turkish banks' lawyer said on Tuesday.
They said the president of the Rotterdam District Court made the decision today after hearing arguments during proceedings last Friday.
ABN AMRO said last week it had closed the accounts of the banks, which operate in the Netherlands as representative offices without banking licences, at the request of the Dutch authorities.
The banks are state-owned Emlakbank and Ziraatbank and privately-owned Akbank and Turkiye Is Bankasi.
Guus Schipper, lawyer for the banks, said the banks had 14 days to appeal but had not yet decided whether to do so.

ABN AMRO said last week the Dutch authorities asked it to close the accounts as the Turkish banks may have breached Dutch banking regulations by collecting money from clients and depositing them in their accounts at ABN AMRO.
But Schipper said the Turkish banks denied any wrongdoing and wanted to have the issue tested in court.
